issue: Wrong outcome: yield pooled over all primary crops (mostly rice, plus wheat, maize, others). It is not a corn or soybean yield, and mixing it into a corn estimate would mostly carry the rice response.
context_note: Quote verified (p.5). Only usable as background: China-wide unweighted meta-analysis, 442 obs / 53 studies, all crops, +9.7%.

The only corn-specific result in the paper: maize after winter legume CCs vs fallow, +27.2 +/- 9.9% (Fig. 7a). The paper gives no maize estimate for winter non-legume or summer legume CCs (Fig. 7b/c), so it is legume-only and likely overstates a general CC effect. Unweighted meta-analysis (only 49 of 442 obs had SD), China. Few winter-CC maize records (paper notes only a few winter CCs before spring maize in the North China Plain), so n is small; per-category n appears only in the Fig. 7 graphic. Whether +/- is a 95% CI half-width or an SE is not stated in the text. No soybean data in this paper.

issue: Not corn-specific: an N-input moderator for primary crop yield pooled over all crops (Fig. 8a). The 23.0% is a model prediction at 0 kg N/ha, not a measured corn or soybean yield effect.
context_note: Quote verified (p.6). Useful qualitatively: the CC yield benefit shrinks as N fertilizer rises (winter legume 23.0 -> 18.5%, winter non-legume 14.0 -> 9.6%, summer legume 8.6 -> 4.6%, from 0 to 100 kg N/ha).
